title: Order the Relay, Find the Brake

scenes.tts: Chapter one separated an itch-producing input from the neurons carrying it. Once those neurons fire, how can experiments order a spinal relay? Carry the same teal pathway from skin into the dorsal horn.
scenes.caption: Chapter 1 separated an itch-producing input from the neurons carrying it. Once those neurons fire, how can experiments order a spinal relay? Carry the same teal pathway from skin into the dorsal horn.
scenes.visual: Reuse chapter 1's colour map exactly: histamine gold, chloroquine blue, itch-route neurons teal, pain-related output red, inhibition purple, neutral tissue white. The existing teal afferent grows from skin into a dorsal-horn cross-section that fills most of the frame. The title appears after the question.
scenes.narration: Chapter 1 separated an itch-producing input from the neurons carrying it. Once those neurons fire, how can experiments order a spinal relay? Carry the same teal pathway from skin into the dorsal horn.

scenes.tts: In one mouse model, the afferent supplies N P P B. Without N P P B, almost all tested itch responses disappeared. Injecting N P P B around the cord itself evoked scratching. The missing signal was upstream; downstream machinery could still respond.
scenes.caption: In one mouse model, the afferent supplies Nppb. Without Nppb, almost all tested itch responses disappeared. Injecting Nppb around the cord itself evoked scratching. The missing signal was upstream; downstream machinery could still respond.
scenes.visual: The teal afferent supplies labelled Nppb blocks along a dotted functional path toward a white NPRA cell. Cross out Nppb; a schematic scratching gauge falls. Then animate an intrathecal syringe beside the cord adding Nppb downstream of the knockout; the same gauge rises.
scenes.narration: In one mouse model, the afferent supplies Nppb. Without Nppb, almost all tested itch responses disappeared. Injecting Nppb around the cord itself evoked scratching. The missing signal was upstream; downstream machinery could still respond.

scenes.tts: Next, researchers removed about seventy percent of spinal cells carrying N P R A. These cells carry the N P P B receptor. If G R P acts later, should added G R P still evoke scratching?
scenes.caption: Next, researchers removed about 70 percent of spinal cells carrying NPRA, the Nppb receptor. If GRP acts later, should added GRP still evoke scratching?
scenes.visual: Carry the relay. Fade roughly seven of ten NPRA-cell icons, with about 70 percent written on screen. Hold a labelled GRP block above the downstream side and ask: Can GRP bypass this loss? Keep the output gauge neutral.
scenes.narration: Next, researchers removed about 70 percent of spinal cells carrying NPRA, the Nppb receptor. If GRP acts later, should added GRP still evoke scratching?

scenes.visual: Hold the bypass question for 4.5 seconds. The GRP block drifts toward the downstream cell but does not land. Reveal no answer.

scenes.tts: It still evoked scratching. The simplest order starts with sensory N P P B, then N P R A cells. G R P and G R P R follow. A downstream signal bypassed loss of the proposed upstream population.
scenes.caption: It still evoked scratching. The simplest order is sensory Nppb, then NPRA cells, then GRP and GRPR. A downstream signal bypassed loss of the proposed upstream population.
scenes.visual: The GRP block lands on a GRPR-labelled cell downstream; the schematic scratching gauge rises. Draw one dotted arrowed sequence across the frame: Nppb to NPRA cells to GRP to GRPR. Label it functional order, not wiring, and highlight the bypass arc around the missing cells.
scenes.narration: It still evoked scratching. The simplest order is sensory Nppb, then NPRA cells, then GRP and GRPR. A downstream signal bypassed loss of the proposed upstream population.

scenes.tts: Independent tests support the later G R P R step. G R P R mutant mice scratched less to tested itch-producing agents. Removing G R P R expressing spinal neurons also lowered scratching, while measured pain behaviours remained.
scenes.caption: Independent tests support the later GRPR step. Grpr-mutant mice scratched less to tested itch-producing agents. Removing GRPR-expressing spinal neurons also lowered scratching, while measured pain behaviours remained.
scenes.visual: Carry the ordered relay. First replace the GRPR cell with a mutant version; then remove it entirely. In both transformations, lower the teal schematic scratching gauge while keeping the red measured-pain gauge level.
scenes.narration: Independent tests support the later GRPR step. Grpr-mutant mice scratched less to tested itch-producing agents. Removing GRPR-expressing spinal neurons also lowered scratching, while measured pain behaviours remained.

scenes.tts: This orders functions, not complete anatomy. The experiments did not show direct synapses. They did not identify one source of G R P. The sequence is one supported route in mice, not every itch route or a human circuit.
scenes.caption: This orders functions, not complete anatomy. The experiments did not show direct synapses. They did not identify one source of GRP. The sequence is one supported route in mice, not every itch route or a human circuit.
scenes.visual: Keep the dotted links labelled functional order. Put question marks over two candidate GRP sources, sensory and spinal. Add a small mouse silhouette beside the model; a human silhouette stays outside a dashed evidence boundary.
scenes.narration: This orders functions, not complete anatomy. The experiments did not show direct synapses. They did not identify one source of GRP. The sequence is one supported route in mice, not every itch route or a human circuit.

scenes.tts: Relays are only half the story. B H L H B five dependent spinal interneurons provide inhibition. Mice missing that developmental population scratched excessively. Removing a brake can raise output without strengthening the incoming itch-producing signal.
scenes.caption: Relays are only half the story. Bhlhb5-dependent spinal interneurons provide inhibition. Mice missing that developmental population scratched excessively. Removing a brake can raise output without strengthening the incoming itch-producing signal.
scenes.visual: Add a large purple inhibitory lever pressing down on the relay's schematic output gauge. Label its cell Bhlhb5-dependent. Remove the lever while keeping the teal input arrows identical; the output gauge rises.
scenes.narration: Relays are only half the story. Bhlhb5-dependent spinal interneurons provide inhibition. Mice missing that developmental population scratched excessively. Removing a brake can raise output without strengthening the incoming itch-producing signal.

scenes.tts: Light touch can use another control route. Removing or silencing N P Y lineage spinal interneurons increased mechanical scratching in one paradigm. Tested chemical itch and pain did not rise. Mechanical scratching also survived G R P R cell ablation there.
scenes.caption: Light touch can use another control route. Removing or silencing NPY-lineage spinal interneurons increased mechanical scratching in one paradigm. Tested chemical itch and pain did not rise. Mechanical scratching also survived GRPR-cell ablation there.
scenes.visual: Branch the carried cord into two lanes. A moving soft filament enters the mechanical lane; gold and blue droplets enter the chemical lane. Remove a purple NPY-lineage gate only from the mechanical lane. Its schematic scratching gauge rises while chemical and red pain gauges hold. Cross out GRPR cells without stopping the mechanical lane.
scenes.narration: Light touch can use another control route. Removing or silencing NPY-lineage spinal interneurons increased mechanical scratching in one paradigm. Tested chemical itch and pain did not rise. Mechanical scratching also survived GRPR-cell ablation there.

scenes.tts: Scratching can feed back too. In primate recordings, scratching suppressed histamine-evoked activity in spinothalamic neurons. It spared baseline and capsaicin-evoked activity. That is a firing measurement, not a reported sensation.
scenes.caption: Scratching can feed back too. In primate recordings, scratching suppressed histamine-evoked activity in spinothalamic neurons. It spared baseline and capsaicin-evoked activity. That is a firing measurement, not a reported sensation.
scenes.visual: Extend the cord output upward as a teal spike train labelled schematic. A scratching paw sends a purple feedback arc. Only the gold histamine-evoked spike train shrinks; baseline and red capsaicin lanes retain their heights. Mark recording, not sensation.
scenes.narration: Scratching can feed back too. In primate recordings, scratching suppressed histamine-evoked activity in spinothalamic neurons. It spared baseline and capsaicin-evoked activity. That is a firing measurement, not a reported sensation.

scenes.tts: The guiding rule now has its full circuit. Trigger, recruited population, spinal route, and inhibition together shape scratching. Use perturbations to order links, but do not mistake functional order for complete wiring.
scenes.caption: The guiding rule now has its full circuit. Trigger, recruited population, spinal route, and inhibition together shape scratching. Use perturbations to order links, but do not mistake functional order for complete wiring.
scenes.visual: Return to the full skin-to-cord world. Gold and blue triggers, teal sensory population, dotted relay and purple gates move gently. A bracket steps across one link at a time, then the model gains a large label: functional order, not complete wiring.
scenes.narration: The guiding rule now has its full circuit. Trigger, recruited population, spinal route, and inhibition together shape scratching. Use perturbations to order links, but do not mistake functional order for complete wiring.

scenes.visual: End card with Hex and the spoken line: Do not mistake functional order for complete wiring. Keep the dotted relay moving faintly behind it.
